key_insight: In small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut achieves mean selection ratios of 0.955–1.000, exceeding the reported depth-one QAOA mean expected ratios.
engineering_relevance: The results motivate testing whether shallow edge-encoding circuits can reduce classical optimization effort for Max-Cut.
method: Encode graph edges with CX–Ry(θ)–CX blocks in a shift-phase circuit.
Evaluate the four leading QASPA bit strings classically and retain the best cut.
Compare against depth-one QAOA with one to ten classical optimization restarts.
evidence_signal: Seed-42 exact state-vector tests cover backbone-augmented random graphs at four additional-edge probabilities and 19 custom unweighted topologies; retained finite-shot checks preserve topology-level readouts under the stated shot rule.
watch_item: QASPA’s best-of-four selection score and QAOA’s expected ratio are different metrics, so these small simulations do not establish an equal-budget or hardware advantage.
paper_title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
